label: Guayaquil — Epicenter of the Conflict
sub: Ecuador's largest city and main Pacific port; epicenter of gang violence, prison unrest, and the January 2024 TC Televisión attack.

label: Litoral Penitentiary — Site of Repeated Massacres
sub: Guayaquil's largest prison, holding roughly 10,000 inmates (2x capacity); site of the 2021 massacre (119 dead) and the November 2024 riot (15-17 dead).

label: Las Malvinas — Site of the 'Guayaquil Four' Abduction
sub: Guayaquil neighborhood under military control where four Afro-Ecuadorian boys were abducted by soldiers on December 8, 2024.

label: Taura — Bodies of 'Guayaquil Four' Found
sub: Marshy area outside an Ecuadorian Air Force base where the charred remains of the four abducted boys were found on December 24, 2024.

label: Durán — Persistent Violence Corridor
sub: Industrial city across the Guayas river from Guayaquil, recording some of Ecuador's highest homicide rates amid gang territorial disputes.

label: Portete — Freddy Kruegers Stronghold
sub: Guayaquil neighborhood where at least 12 murders were reported in the days following the November 2024 Litoral Penitentiary massacre, tied to the Freddy Kruegers gang's presence.

label: Esmeraldas — Trafficking Corridor to Colombia
sub: Northern port province bordering Colombia, under repeated states of emergency; site of the May 2024 double car bombing and the September 2025 prison riot.

label: Quinindé — Journalist Patricio Aguilar Murdered
sub: Esmeraldas province town where community journalist Patricio Aguilar was murdered on March 4, 2025, after reporting on local gang violence.

label: San Lorenzo — Colombia Border Trafficking Route
sub: Border town on the Ecuador-Colombia frontier, a key transit point for cocaine and armed groups including ex-FARC dissidents.

label: Manta — Eloy Alfaro Air Base, US Deployment Site
sub: Former US Forward Operating Location (2000-2009); site of the first acknowledged return of US Air Force personnel for joint intelligence and interdiction training in 2025, and of Fito's June 2025 recapture in a nearby underground bunker.

label: Machala — 14 Killed in Prison Riot
sub: El Oro province capital, site of a September 22, 2025 prison riot that killed 14 inmates, three days before the deadlier Esmeraldas riot.

label: Riobamba — Los Lobos Leader's Prison Escape
sub: Central highlands city where Los Lobos leader Fabricio Colón Pico escaped prison on January 9, 2024, compounding the crisis triggered by Fito's escape two days earlier.

label: Quito — Seat of Government, Diplomatic Engagements
sub: Ecuador's capital and seat of government; site of Noboa's emergency decrees, referendum votes, and diplomatic engagements including the August 2025 visit by DHS Secretary Kristi Noem.

label: Posorja — New Deep-Water Port Trafficking Hub
sub: Deep-water port near Guayaquil that emerged as a major cocaine trafficking node; authorities seized over 15 tons of cocaine tied to the port in 2024 alone, nearly triple the 2023 total.

label: Santa Elena — El Encuentro Mega-Prison
sub: Site of the new El Encuentro maximum-security prison, which received its first transfer of 300 inmates on November 11, 2025, part of a program to build capacity for 12,000 inmates nationwide.

label: Naportec Port Terminal, Guayaquil
sub: Container port terminal where Ecuadorian police seized nearly 700 kilos of cocaine hidden in Noboa family banana shipments between 2020 and 2022, according to leaked police intelligence documents.

label: Manabí Province — Bridge Bombings
sub: Site of October 2025 bridge explosions blamed on a local criminal gang and Colombian ex-FARC dissidents, in retaliation for a military crackdown on illegal mining.

label: Guayaquil — Shopping Mall Car Bombing
sub: Site of the October 14, 2025 car bomb attack outside a Guayaquil shopping mall that killed one person and led police to defuse a second explosive-laden vehicle nearby.

label: Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas
sub: Province placed under the June 2026 state of emergency amid a nationwide surge in cartel-linked violence.

label: Sucumbíos — Amazon Border Trafficking Route
sub: Oil-producing Amazon province bordering Colombia, included in the June 2026 state of emergency as trafficking and violence spread beyond the coast.

label: Los Ríos Province
sub: Agricultural province in the state of emergency zone declared June 17, 2026, reflecting the spread of gang violence beyond Guayaquil into surrounding provinces.

label: Cuenca / Azuay — Violence Spreads to the Southern Highlands
sub: Historically safer southern highlands province placed under the June 2026 state of emergency, illustrating the geographic spread of the conflict beyond its coastal origins.

label: Pichincha Province — Quito's Home Province
sub: Province containing the capital Quito, included in the June 2026 state of emergency as violence indicators worsened even in traditionally lower-crime areas.

label: El Oro Province
sub: Southern coastal province and site of the Machala prison riot; placed under the June 2026 state of emergency.

label: Guayas Province — Highest Internal Displacement
sub: Ecuador's most populous coastal province, source of the largest share of the roughly 132,000 people displaced internally by gang violence since 2021.

label: Tulcán — Northern Border Displacement Route
sub: Border crossing to Colombia used by Ecuadorians fleeing gang violence and by traffickers moving cocaine and arms in the opposite direction.

label: Babahoyo — Los Ríos Province Gang Clash
sub: Los Ríos provincial capital where four alleged Los Lobos members were killed in a Los Choneros raid on August 16, 2026, amid the gangs' ongoing turf war.

label: Flor de Bastión — Triple Child Killing
sub: Nueva Prosperina neighborhood in Guayaquil where three minors, including a 7-year-old, were shot dead during an August 14, 2026 home invasion.

label: Manta — Prosecutor Alexandra Bravo Assassinated
sub: Flavio Reyes Avenue in central Manta, where prosecutor Gloria Alexandra Bravo Cedeño and her sister were shot dead on June 14, 2026; the third prosecutor assassinated in Manta since 2022.

label: Manta — Home Port of Vessels Targeted in Alleged Covert US Drone Strikes
sub: Home port of the Ecuadorian tuna/fishing fleet; the Fiorella, Negra Francisca Duarte II, and Don Maca — all reportedly struck by drones roughly 170 miles offshore near the Galápagos (outside this map's bounds) in Jan–Mar 2026 — sailed from Manta-area ports. NYT/Washington Post reporting links the strikes to a covert US program; the Pentagon and CIA deny or decline to confirm involvement.
